<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916474_theRebbe_113" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916474_theRebbe_113__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Introductory header with date and abbreviation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B"Sd,</t>
    <t s="1">10 Shevat,</t>
    <t s="2">5711*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The Rebbe writes that the maamar was composed by his father-in-law, the Previous Rebbe, for the day of his histalkus.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Written by the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Admor1,</t>
    <t s="1">in his maamar for the day of his histalkus,</t>
    <t s="2">10 Shevat 5710:</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Explains the phrase "I came to My garden" from the Midrash, focusing on the precise meaning of "Shechinah" and its root in the revelation of Ein Sof.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"I came to My garden, My sister, My bride"2,</t>
    <t s="1">and it is brought in Midrash Rabbah</t>
    <t s="2">(in its place3)</t>
    <t s="3">"It does not say 'to the garden' but 'to My garden,'</t>
    <t s="4">to My private garden,</t>
    <t s="5">to the place which was My essential [dwelling] initially,</t>
    <t s="6">for the essential Shechinah was in the lower realms."</t>
    <t s="7">End of quote.</t>
    <t s="8">And to understand the precise wording "essential Shechinah,"</t>
    <t s="9">behold, in the explanation of "Shechinah," the Alter Rebbea explains</t>
    <t s="10">that it is called Shechinah because it dwells and is enclothed,</t>
    <t s="11">from the term "and I will dwell in their midst"4,</t>
    <t s="12">which is the beginning of the revelation of Ein Sof.</t>
    <t s="13">And from what he writes5</t>
    <t s="14">that the beginning of the revelation of Ein Sof is called by the name Shechinah,</t>
    <t s="15">it is understood from this that the concept of Shechinah is also far above Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="16">even in the aspect of the light before the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="17">for the beginning of revelation is in the light of Ein Sof before the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="18">and as the Mitteler Rebbe wroteb</t>
    <t s="19">that the illumination of the line and thread relative to the essentiality of Ein Sof is called by the name Shechinah.</t>
    <t s="20">For the concept of Shechinah is in every place according to its context.</t>
    <t s="21">Regarding Atzilus, Malchus is called by the name Shechinah.</t>
    <t s="22">And also in this, that Malchus of Atzilus is called Shechinah, the Tzemach Tzedekc explains</t>
    <t s="23">that this is specifically when it becomes an aspect of Atik for the world of Beriah,</t>
    <t s="24">but when it is in Atzilus it is unified with them</t>
    <t s="25">(with the Sefiros of Atzilus)</t>
    <t s="26">and the term Shechinah does not apply.</t>
    <t s="27">Nevertheless, this does not contradict what was said above that the line is called by the name Shechinah,</t>
    <t s="28">for the Shechinah mentioned in the words of our sages is Malchus of Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="29">and even this is only when it specifically becomes an aspect of Atik for Beriah,</t>
    <t s="30">but in its root,</t>
    <t s="31">that is, as it is relative to Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="32">behold, even the line is called by the name Shechinah.</t>
    <t s="33">And one of the reasons why the line is called by the name Shechinah relative to Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="34">the Rebbe Maharashd wrote</t>
    <t s="35">is that the line, the intent of its drawing down is in order to be enclothed in the worlds and souls of Israel,</t>
    <t s="36">therefore, even at its beginning it is called by the name Shechinah.</t>
    <t s="37">And higher still, the Shechinah in its first root above the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="38">the Rebbe, of blessed memorye, explains</t>
    <t s="39">that the revelation of the light as it is before the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="40">is called by the name Shechinah.</t>
    <t s="41">For in the general light before the tzimtzum there are three levels,</t>
    <t s="42">the essence of the light and the spreading forth of the light,</t>
    <t s="43">and in the spreading forth of the light there are two levels: the revelation of the light as it is for itself, which is the source of the light of Sovev,</t>
    <t s="44">and the revelation of the light for itself that relates to the worlds, which is the source of the light of Memaleh,</t>
    <t s="45">and this revelation of light is called by the name Shechinah.</t>
    <t s="46">And even though it is before the tzimtzum and it is impossible for it to be a source for worlds,</t>
    <t s="47">which is why the tzimtzum was necessary,</t>
    <t s="48">and the first tzimtzum is specifically in the aspect of withdrawal,</t>
    <t s="49">nevertheless, it is called by the name Shechinah.</t>
    <t s="50">And this is the precise wording "the essential Shechinah was in the lower realms,"</t>
    <t s="51">that is, the revelation of the Shechinah in the lower realms</t>
    <t s="52">is not the Shechinah as it is relative to Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="53">that is, Malchus,</t>
    <t s="54">nor as it is relative to Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="55">that is, the line,</t>
    <t s="56">but rather the essence and pnimiyus of the Shechinah was specifically in the lower realms,</t>
    <t s="57">for the light</t>
    <t s="58">that is enclothed in the worlds comes in order and gradation.</t>
    <t s="59">And above, it shines with greater revelation,</t>
    <t s="60">and the more it is drawn down and descends, the light diminishes.</t>
    <t s="61">And so it is in general regarding the light of the order of hishtalshelus.</t>
    <t s="62">And even though before the sin there was also below the light in revelation,</t>
    <t s="63">nevertheless, even then the revelation of the light was greater above.</t>
    <t s="64">And as our sages said*vi,</t>
    <t s="65">"He extended His right hand and created the heavens, He extended His left hand and created the earth."</t>
    <t s="66">Rather, the intent is regarding the light that is above the worlds,</t>
    <t s="67">the essential Shechinah.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
